# LIV (nightclub)

LIV is a world-renowned nightclub located within the Fontainebleau Miami Beach hotel on Collins Avenue in Miami Beach, Florida , . Founded and operated by David Grutman through his company Groot Hospitality, LIV has established itself as a premier destination for luxury nightlife, consistently ranking among the top venues globally , . Its identity is deeply intertwined with the historical legacy of its location, which previously hosted iconic mid-century entertainment venues like the La Ronde Room, and its relentless pursuit of technological innovation in its design and production , . The venue operates as a cornerstone of an integrated hospitality ecosystem managed by Groot Hospitality, which also includes other high-profile properties such as Story nightclub and Komodo restaurant , . Following its successful launch in Miami, the LIV brand was expanded to the Las Vegas Strip, opening inside the Fontainebleau Las Vegas resort in December 2023, demonstrating the franchise's appeal in one of the world's most competitive nightlife markets [), ]. Throughout its history, LIV has been a focal point of celebrity culture, frequently hosting international clientele and global music stars, but it has also been the site of numerous high-profile incidents, ranging from public feuds to serious criminal allegations, contributing to its complex and controversial reputation , , . The club’s powerful brand has also led it into legal battles over trademark protection, notably filing a notice of opposition against "LIV Golf" in 2023 to prevent consumer confusion .

## History and Location

The history of LIV nightclub is inseparable from the rich cultural tapestry of Miami Beach and the specific location it occupies. The venue opened in 2008 as the crown jewel of the Fontainebleau Hotel's ambitious billion-dollar renovation, a project designed to honor the original work of architect Morris Lapidus , , . This strategic positioning was crucial; the Fontainebleau Miami Beach, which first opened its doors in 1954, has long been an icon of the city's Art Deco heritage and a hub for glamour and entertainment . LIV was not merely added to the hotel; it was conceived as its centerpiece, designed to attract a new generation of elite clientele while paying homage to the property's storied past . The name "LIV" itself is a deliberate nod to this history, using the Roman numeral for fifty-four (LIV) to commemorate the year the original Fontainebleau hotel opened . This clever branding immediately connected the modern club to a legacy of post-war American excess and celebrity.

The space LIV now occupies holds a profound historical significance that predates even the original 1954 hotel. It was originally the site of the Copa Room in the 1940s, which later became the Tropigala Lounge after the hotel's 1960s expansion , . However, its most famous incarnation was the La Ronde Room, which operated from the 1950s through the 1960s , . This venue was a veritable who's who of mid-century American entertainment, featuring performances from legendary figures such as Frank Sinatra, Sammy Davis Jr., Ann Miller, Elvis Presley, and Tony Bennett , , . Frank Sinatra was the very first performer to grace the stage of what would become LIV, setting a precedent for the caliber of talent that would be associated with the location for decades , . By situating LIV within this historic context, its founders created a narrative of continuity, positioning the modern club not just as a new establishment but as a direct heir to a tradition of world-class performance and star power . This deep-rooted history provides a unique foundation for LIV's identity, blending contemporary luxury with the nostalgic glamour of Miami's golden era.

The grand opening of LIV in 2008 was a highly symbolic event that cemented its status as a major player in the global nightlife scene. The venue hosted the after-party for the Victoria's Secret Fashion Show, an event attended by A-list celebrities and broadcast to millions, immediately signaling LIV's connection to the highest echelons of fashion and celebrity culture , . This inaugural event set the tone for the club's future, establishing a standard of exclusivity and spectacle that has been maintained ever since. Owner David Grutman articulated this vision early on, stating that "each night since, we’ve continued to change production and create a new party on a nightly basis," highlighting a commitment to constant reinvention and maintaining its edge as a premier destination . The venue's architecture, particularly its iconic domed ceiling, has been a central element of this evolving experience. The dome, which spans approximately 88 feet, was already a feature of the pre-renovation space, containing over 800 LED fixtures and intelligent lighting designed to create dynamic visual effects . This architectural centerpiece, combined with state-of-the-art sound systems and a vibrant atmosphere, transformed the former La Ronde Room into a technologically advanced and luxurious party environment , . Over the years, LIV has consistently reinforced its position as a leader in nightlife production, undergoing significant renovations to enhance its technological infrastructure and spatial design, thereby solidifying its role as a pioneer in redefining the modern nightclub experience in Miami Beach .

## Ownership and Business Ecosystem

The identity and success of LIV nightclub are inextricably linked to its founder, David Grutman, and the sophisticated business ecosystem he has cultivated around his ventures , . Grutman is consistently identified as the visionary force behind LIV, having founded the original MMG Nightlife, which later evolved into Groot Hospitality, the company that owns and operates the venue [), ]. His leadership extends beyond mere ownership; he is the creative director whose personal investment, both financial and emotional, has been a driving factor in the club's evolution. During the challenging period of the COVID-19 pandemic, Grutman publicly expressed the immense personal toll of the club's closure, describing LIV as his "lifeblood" and refusing to reopen under substandard conditions, a testament to his deep-seated commitment to the brand's quality and prestige . This hands-on approach defines his operational philosophy, which prioritizes creating an unparalleled party experience and constantly pushing the boundaries of what a nightclub can offer .

Grutman's career trajectory reveals a shrewd businessman navigating the complexities of the entertainment industry. In 2013, he sold an 80% stake in his company to Robert F. X. Sillerman's SFX, a move that temporarily removed him from direct control [)]. However, when SFX filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2016, Grutman successfully reacquired full control by 2018, reorganizing the business into Groot Hospitality [)]. This resilience highlights his ability to manage corporate challenges and maintain his vision for his brands. A pivotal moment in the club's development came in 2019, when Groot Hospitality sold a majority 51% stake to Live Nation Entertainment for $25.5 million, at which time the company was valued at $50 million [), ]. This partnership represents a strategic alliance between Grutman's creative and experiential expertise and Live Nation's vast resources, industry connections, and marketing prowess. Under this arrangement, Live Nation holds the controlling 51% share, while Grutman's Groot Hospitality retains 49%, ensuring his continued influence while leveraging Live Nation's power to expand the LIV brand's reach and impact [)].

LIV does not operate in isolation but is a central component of a larger, integrated hospitality conglomerate built by Grutman. Through Groot Hospitality, he oversees a diverse portfolio of venues that cater to various tastes and occasions, creating a cohesive lifestyle brand . This ecosystem includes the adjacent Story nightclub, which offers a different, more intimate vibe, as well as a collection of restaurants that range from fine dining to casual fare, such as Komodo, Swan Miami, Papi Steak, and Gekkō , . This vertical integration creates a powerful synergy; guests can transition seamlessly from a gourmet dinner at Komodo to dancing at LIV, maximizing their engagement with Grutman's brand and increasing lifetime customer value . The partnership with Fontainebleau Development further enhances this model, creating a unified experience where patrons entering via guest lists or general admission tickets can be nurtured into high-spend VIP clients, often through stays at the affiliated Fontainebleau hotel . This strategy exemplifies a long-term focus on building a loyal customer base within a curated ecosystem.

Beyond its commercial operations, Grutman has institutionalized his brand and ethos through education, further cementing LIV's place in Miami's cultural landscape. He teaches a course titled "The David Grutman Experience" at Florida International University's Chaplin School of Hospitality & Tourism Management, drawing on his real-world successes to educate the next generation of hospitality leaders , . The school explicitly cites Fontainebleau Miami Beach, home to LIV®, as a key industry partner, alongside major corporations like Marriott International and Carnival Corporation, reinforcing LIV's recognition as a world-renowned venue within elite academic and professional circles , , . This partnership allows students to gain experiential learning directly at Grutman's venues, fostering a pipeline of talent familiar with his brand's standards and vision . This multifaceted approach—combining a founder-centric brand, a strategic corporate partnership, an integrated hospitality ecosystem, and a commitment to education—has been instrumental in transforming LIV from a single nightclub into a powerful and enduring cultural institution.

## The Miami Venue: Description and Renovations

The LIV nightclub in Miami is defined by its opulent design, cutting-edge technology, and strict adherence to an ultra-exclusive atmosphere. Located on the ground level of the Fontainebleau Miami Beach hotel at 4441 Collins Avenue, the venue spans a vast area, with sources citing dimensions of over 18,000 square feet or up to 22,000 square feet, accommodating a capacity of approximately 1,000 to 1,100 guests , , . The space is designed as a dual-level environment, combining a lively main dance floor with a more elevated VIP area, accessible via a glowing staircase . Guests must be at least 21 years old and present a valid U.S. driver's license or passport upon entry; foreign government IDs are not accepted , . The club enforces a stringent dress code, prohibiting casual attire such as tank tops, sleeveless t-shirts, shorts, flip-flops, and athletic wear, with entry remaining at the discretion of the doormen . This selective policy ensures a certain standard of decorum and contributes to the venue's high-end ambiance. Operations are primarily concentrated Thursday through Sunday, running from 11:00 PM until 5:00 AM, although the space is available for private bookings seven days a week , .

At the heart of LIV's design is its signature architectural feature: the iconic dome . Before its major renovation, the dome housed an impressive array of lighting technology, including approximately 585 Philips Color Kinetics iColor Cove MX units embedded in channels radiating from the center, and perimeter-washing fixtures, all controlled by a sophisticated e:cue Media Engine 2 system . This setup allowed for a wide range of choreographed light shows that could be manipulated by a light jockey to match the rhythm of the music, transforming the entire space into a dynamic sensory environment . The venue also boasts a state-of-the-art L-Acoustics L Series sound system, multiple in-house video screens, and six private skyboxes offering premium table service and exclusive views of the dance floor , . This combination of advanced audiovisual technology and luxurious amenities has made LIV a benchmark for modern nightclub production .

A landmark event in the venue's recent history was a comprehensive $10 million renovation that took place during the summer of 2024, resulting in a nearly nine-week closure , , . This extensive upgrade was overseen by the acclaimed experiential design firm ICRAVE, with Steve Lieberman of SJ Lighting playing a key role , . The primary objective was to reaffirm LIV's position as a global leader in nightlife by introducing groundbreaking technology and enhancing the overall guest experience , . The centerpiece of the renovation was the installation of a custom-built, kinetic LED ceiling affectionately nicknamed "The Spider" , . This seven-legged, steel truss structure, which alone cost an estimated $3 million, contains 410 individual moving LED panels, each capable of rotating at one foot per second in sync with the music , . The Spider is equipped with integrated fans that blow air onto the audience below, adding a tactile dimension to the auditory and visual spectacle . The renovation also included the addition of over 400 digitally controlled LED panels throughout the venue, new marble floors, granite countertops, revamped banquettes, and rotating art installations by local Miami street artists , , . This transformative project underscored LIV's commitment to constant reinvention, aiming to create a truly immersive and unforgettable party experience that sets a new standard for the industry .

The reopening following the 2024 renovation marked a significant milestone, celebrated with a "Sneak Peek Weekend" that featured headlining performances by Travis Scott and Skrillex, signaling a new era for the club , . The official grand opening was scheduled for early October 2024, confirming that the venue was fully operational and ready to welcome back its elite clientele . This reopening coincided with the start of LIV's tenth season, celebrating a decade of continuous operation since its 2008 debut , . The timing was strategically chosen to capitalize on the peak Miami tourism season, with new programming introduced, including open-format Fridays, dedicated dance music Saturdays, and "LIV On Sunday" positioned as "the biggest hip-hop party in the world" . The venue continues to host major events throughout the year, including Miami Music Week and Art Basel, featuring a roster of the world's top DJs and performers such as DJ Khaled, John Summit, Tiësto, and Lil Wayne, ensuring its relevance and prominence in the global entertainment calendar , , , .

## The Las Vegas Venue

Building on the proven success and strong brand recognition of the Miami flagship, David Grutman embarked on a significant expansion by launching a second LIV nightclub in Las Vegas. This venture, situated inside the newly constructed Fontainebleau Las Vegas resort, marked a strategic move to replicate the LIV formula in one of the most competitive and saturated nightlife markets in the world [), ]. The Fontainebleau Las Vegas itself is a monumental $3.7 billion development, and its grand opening on December 13, 2023, provided the perfect platform for the arrival of its crown jewel nightclub . The launch of LIV Las Vegas was not a simple transplant but a carefully orchestrated expansion that aimed to blend the core elements of the Miami concept with the unique energy of the Las Vegas Strip. Grutman emphasized that artists like resident DJs John Summit and Metro Boomin were involved in the construction phase, making them personally invested in the club's success and ensuring a product that reflected their artistic vision .

The LIV Las Vegas venue opened its doors in 2024, quickly establishing itself as a key player in the city's entertainment circuit . The club operates on a schedule tailored to the Las Vegas market, typically open from Friday to Sunday, from 10:30 p.m. to 4:00 a.m. . From its inception, LIV Las Vegas has focused on delivering an elevated hospitality experience, integrating state-of-the-art lighting and sound systems to compete with the Strip's other mega-clubs . The venue has attracted a steady stream of high-profile talent, with resident DJs such as John Summit, Metro Boomin, Cloonee, and Dom Dolla performing regularly, alongside special appearances by major artists . This programming strategy mirrors the successful model employed in Miami, creating a consistent draw for music lovers and club-goers. The venue has also become a magnet for celebrities, welcoming visitors like Bad Bunny during Super Bowl weekend and *Vanderpump Rules* star James Kennedy, who performed as LIV's internationally recognized resident DJ . This association with celebrity culture helps to generate buzz and reinforces the club's image as a must-visit destination for anyone on the Strip.

The expansion into Las Vegas was not just about opening a new location; it was about extending Grutman's integrated business ecosystem to a new market. Similar to the synergy between LIV and the Fontainebleau Miami Beach hotel, the Las Vegas LIV is part of a larger integrated ecosystem that includes other Groot Hospitality properties co-located within the resort, such as the restaurants Papi Steak and Komodo . This model allows for cross-promotion and creates a cohesive lifestyle brand where guests can dine and then transition to the nightclub, maximizing revenue opportunities and enhancing the overall guest experience. Michael Waltman, Executive Vice President of Fontainebleau Development, highlighted this integrated approach, explaining how the resort aims to capture guests at every stage of their lifecycle, from college attendees entering via guest lists to becoming high-spending VIP clients . This strategic alignment with the parent company's broader goals demonstrates a well-thought-out plan for sustainable growth and profitability in a hyper-competitive environment.

The launch of LIV Las Vegas represented a significant validation of the LIV brand model. Successfully adapting the Miami concept to the unique demands of the Las Vegas market proved that the core elements of the brand—luxury, cutting-edge technology, and a focus on top-tier musical talent—were transferable and highly appealing to a new audience. The timing of the opening, coinciding with the grand opening of the entire Fontainebleau Las Vegas resort, ensured maximum visibility and media attention, with the initial event featuring A-list celebrities such as Kim Kardashian, Cher, Sylvester Stallone, Lenny Kravitz, Bryan Cranston, Aaron Paul, and Tom Brady . This star-studded debut sent a clear message to the industry that LIV was not just another club but a major new player poised to make a significant impact. As of early 2025, LIV Las Vegas remains a prominent fixture on the Strip, continuing to host resident DJs and headline acts, solidifying its status as a key component of the LIV global brand and a testament to David Grutman's vision for scalable, high-end nightlife experiences . The venue underwent a months-long renovation, closing November 2024 and reopening March 2025, indicating a continued commitment to maintaining its competitive edge [)].

## Cultural Impact and Controversies

LIV nightclub has carved out a distinct and influential niche in the global cultural landscape, functioning as a nexus for celebrity culture, high-energy entertainment, and, at times, high-profile controversy. Its reputation as a magnet for international clientele and global celebrities is well-documented, with names like Drake, Rihanna, Paris Hilton, and Bad Bunny frequently cited as regular patrons , . This concentration of fame creates a self-perpetuating cycle of allure; the presence of celebrities attracts more celebrities and media attention, which in turn drives demand from the general public seeking to witness or participate in the spectacle. LIV has served as a backdrop for countless events, from corporate-sponsored fashion shows for brands like Adidas to elaborate multi-day celebrations for major cultural festivals like Miami Art Week and Miami Music Week, further cementing its status as a central hub of Miami's social and entertainment scene , , , , . The club's ability to consistently attract and host the world's top DJs and performers, such as Calvin Harris, Diddy, and Machine Gun Kelly, underscores its role as a premier venue for live music and dance culture , , .

However, LIV's glamorous facade has been punctuated by a series of notable incidents that have contributed to its controversial reputation. The club has been the site of several high-profile public feuds and altercations. One of the earliest documented incidents involved rapper Dan Blizerian allegedly kicking a woman in the face in December 2014 . Another involved a public escalation of tensions between rappers Birdman and Lil Wayne, which culminated in water bottles being thrown at Jim Jones’ birthday party . Perhaps the most widely reported incident occurred outside the club in December 2014, when Sean "Diddy" Combs allegedly punched Drake over a dispute concerning the beat for Drake's hit song '0 to 100'. While Combs vehemently denied the allegation, calling Drake his friend, the incident became a major tabloid story and was widely attributed to the LIV venue, further linking the club to celebrity drama , . These events, along with others like Joaquin Phoenix's rap performance tied to his *I'm Still Here* performance art project, paint a picture of LIV as a place where the line between entertainment and reality can blur, leading to unpredictable and sometimes volatile situations .

Perhaps the most serious documented controversy associated with LIV involves allegations of violent assault. On November 9, 2024, Miami-based artist and club promoter Prince alleged that rapper Tory Lanez assaulted him inside the LIV nightclub . According to Prince, the altercation, which originated from a misinterpreted Instagram post, escalated into a brutal attack captured on cellphone video, showing Lanez punching, stomping, and jumping on Prince. The assault resulted in a dislodged tooth requiring multiple medical procedures and ongoing anxiety for the victim . Prince's attorney characterized Lanez's conduct as a "chronic problem," and the case proceeded to litigation after failed settlement attempts . This incident places LIV at the center of a significant legal matter and highlights the club's association with artists facing serious criminal charges. The controversy was amplified by Megan Thee Stallion's separate accusation against Lanez in July 2024, where she alleged he shot her after a party in Los Angeles, suggesting a troubling pattern of alleged behavior that has drawn scrutiny to the environments where these artists perform .

More recently, LIV has continued to be a stage for spontaneous and unexpected events. In December 2025, pop superstar Shakira performed an impromptu set at the club, only to abruptly end her performance after reportedly discovering that fans were filming up her dress . An official statement from the club attributed the interruption to Shakira's own photo/video team filming without consent during an informal crowd interaction, rather than fan behavior, but the incident nonetheless showcased the unpredictable nature of events at the venue . This mix of world-class entertainment, intense celebrity culture, and recurring controversies makes LIV a compelling and complex subject of cultural analysis. It serves not only as a destination for leisure and celebration but also as a microcosm of the pressures, rivalries, and potential dangers inherent in the high-stakes world of modern celebrity and nightlife.

## Brand Identity and Trademark Dispute

The "LIV" brand is a potent and valuable asset, built over more than a decade of association with luxury, celebrity, and high-energy entertainment. Its identity is so strong that it has transcended its function as a nightclub name to become a recognizable symbol within the hospitality and entertainment industries. This strength was formally acknowledged in 2023 when the owners of LIV took legal action to protect their intellectual property from a potentially confusing competitor. On March 15, 2023, LIV Miami filed a Notice of Opposition with the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) to block the trademark registration of "LIV Golf" . This legal maneuver revealed the commercial significance attached to the four-letter moniker and demonstrated the proactive stance taken by the LIV brand's management to defend its market identity.

In its official filing, LIV argued that the marks "LIV" and "LIV Golf" are confusingly similar not only visually and phonetically but also aurally, creating a high risk of consumer confusion . The opposition specifically cited the shared use of the term "LIV" and pointed to a common perception among consumers that both brands are connected to the same entity, given the overlapping nature of their target audiences. LIV's services, centered on nightlife and entertainment, and LIV Golf's services, related to professional golf, were deemed to share an overlapping consumer base, which could lead to the erroneous belief that one brand endorsed or was otherwise associated with the other . This argument is a standard tactic in trademark law used to prevent dilution of a famous mark and to stop competitors from capitalizing on an existing brand's goodwill. The case was pending at the time of the article's publication, highlighting the ongoing legal efforts to safeguard the LIV brand's integrity and commercial value .

The origins of the LIV brand name are themselves a key component of its identity, rooted in the history of the Fontainebleau Miami Beach hotel. As previously noted, the name "LIV" is the Roman numeral for fifty-four (L=50, I=1, V=5), a direct reference to the year 1954, when the original Fontainebleau hotel opened . This clever wordplay connects the modern nightclub to the property's foundational history, giving the brand a sense of longevity and heritage that distinguishes it from newer establishments. This historical link is a cornerstone of LIV's marketing and storytelling, reinforcing its position as a timeless yet modern institution in Miami's entertainment scene. The brand is officially registered with the trademark symbol (®), as seen in its partnership descriptions with institutions like Florida International University, which refers to it as "LIV® nightclub" , . This formal registration underscores the brand's legal standing and the seriousness with which its owners treat its protection.

Beyond its legal protections and historical roots, the LIV brand is synonymous with a specific type of experience—a world-class nightlife destination that combines state-of-the-art technology with an exclusive, glamorous atmosphere. Rankings from publications such as Rolling Stone Magazine, which named it one of the best dance clubs in America, and Nightclub & Bar Magazine, which ranked it #5 in its 2014 list of the Top 100 Best Clubs in the Country, provide third-party validation of its quality and appeal . Askmen.com went further, ranking it as the #2 best club in the world at one point . These accolades, combined with its consistent billing as "Miami's ultimate nightlife destination" and a venue that "consistently hosts top artists and global celebrities," build a powerful brand identity that is instantly recognizable to those within the industry and aspirational to a global audience . The brand's identity is thus a composite of its tangible assets—its prime location, its innovative technology, and its successful business model—as well as its intangible qualities: its historical narrative, its exclusive clientele, and its powerful association with the pinnacle of popular culture. The decision to litigate against LIV Golf is a clear indication that the owners understand the immense value of this carefully constructed identity and are prepared to defend it vigorously.

Grutman's refusal to reopen under substandard conditions is a testament to his deep-seated commitment to the brand's quality and prestige.
David Grutman's hands-on approach defines his operational philosophy, which prioritizes creating an unparalleled party experience and constantly pushing the boundaries of what a nightclub can offer.
Grutman's career trajectory reveals a shrewd businessman navigating the complexities of the entertainment industry.
In 2013, David Grutman sold an 80% stake in his company to Robert F. X. Sillerman's SFX, a move that temporarily removed him from direct control.
When SFX filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in 2016, Grutman successfully reacquired full control by 2018, reorganizing the business into Groot Hospitality.
This resilience highlights Grutman's ability to manage corporate challenges and maintain his vision for his brands.
A pivotal moment in the club's development came in 2019, when Groot Hospitality sold a majority 51% stake to Live Nation Entertainment for $25.5 million.
At the time of the 2019 sale, Groot Hospitality was valued at $50 million.

The partnership between Groot Hospitality and Live Nation Entertainment represents a strategic alliance between Grutman's creative and experiential expertise and Live Nation's vast resources, industry connections, and marketing prowess.
Under this arrangement, Live Nation holds the controlling 51% share of Groot Hospitality.
Grutman's Groot Hospitality retains 49% ownership, ensuring his continued influence while leveraging Live Nation's power to expand the LIV brand's reach and impact.
LIV does not operate in isolation but is a central component of a larger, integrated hospitality conglomerate built by Grutman.
Through Groot Hospitality, David Grutman oversees a diverse portfolio of venues that cater to various tastes and occasions, creating a cohesive lifestyle brand.
This ecosystem includes the adjacent Story nightclub, which offers a different, more intimate vibe.
The Groot Hospitality ecosystem also includes a collection of restaurants that range from fine dining to casual fare, such as Komodo, Swan Miami, Papi Steak, and Gekkō.
This vertical integration creates a powerful synergy.
Guests can transition seamlessly from a gourmet dinner at Komodo to dancing at LIV, maximizing their engagement with Grutman's brand and increasing lifetime customer value.
The partnership with Fontainebleau Development further enhances this model, creating a unified experience.
Patrons entering via guest lists or general admission tickets can be nurtured into high-spend VIP clients, often through stays at the affiliated Fontainebleau hotel.
This strategy exemplifies a long-term focus on building a loyal customer base within a curated ecosystem.
Beyond its commercial operations, Grutman has institutionalized his brand and ethos through education, further cementing LIV's place in Miami's cultural landscape.
David Grutman teaches a course titled "The David Grutman Experience" at Florida International University's Chaplin School of Hospitality & Tourism Management.
The course draws on Grutman's real-world successes to educate the next generation of hospitality leaders.
Florida International University's Chaplin School explicitly cites Fontainebleau Miami Beach, home to LIV®, as a key industry partner.
LIV is recognized as a world-renowned venue within elite academic and professional circles, alongside major corporations like Marriott International and Carnival Corporation.
This partnership allows students to gain experiential learning directly at Grutman's venues, fostering a pipeline of talent familiar with his brand's standards and vision.

This multifaceted approach—combining a founder-centric brand, a strategic corporate partnership, an integrated hospitality ecosystem, and a commitment to education—has been instrumental in transforming LIV from a single nightclub into a powerful and enduring cultural institution.
The LIV nightclub in Miami is defined by its opulent design, cutting-edge technology, and strict adherence to an ultra-exclusive atmosphere.
LIV is located on the ground level of the Fontainebleau Miami Beach hotel at 4441 Collins Avenue.
The LIV venue spans a vast area, with sources citing dimensions of over 18,000 square feet or up to 22,000 square feet.
LIV accommodates a capacity of approximately 1,000 to 1,100 guests.
The LIV space is designed as a dual-level environment, combining a lively main dance floor with a more elevated VIP area, accessible via a glowing staircase.
Guests must be at least 21 years old and present a valid U.S. driver's license or passport upon entry to LIV.
Foreign government IDs are not accepted at LIV.
The club enforces a stringent dress code, prohibiting casual attire such as tank tops, sleeveless t-shirts, shorts, flip-flops, and athletic wear.
Entry to LIV remains at the discretion of the doormen.
This selective policy ensures a certain standard of decorum and contributes to the venue's high-end ambiance.
LIV operations are primarily concentrated Thursday through Sunday, running from 11:00 PM until 5:00 AM.
The LIV space is available for private bookings seven days a week.
At the heart of LIV's design is its signature architectural feature: the iconic dome.
Before its major renovation, the dome housed an impressive array of lighting technology.
The dome's lighting technology included approximately 585 Philips Color Kinetics iColor Cove MX units embedded in channels radiating from the center, and perimeter-washing fixtures.
All lighting in the dome was controlled by a sophisticated e:cue Media Engine 2 system.

This setup allowed for a wide range of choreographed light shows that could be manipulated by a light jockey to match the rhythm of the music, transforming the entire space into a dynamic sensory environment.
The LIV venue also boasts a state-of-the-art L-Acoustics L Series sound system.
The LIV venue has multiple in-house video screens.
The LIV venue has six private skyboxes offering premium table service and exclusive views of the dance floor.
This combination of advanced audiovisual technology and luxurious amenities has made LIV a benchmark for modern nightclub production.
A landmark event in LIV's recent history was a comprehensive $10 million renovation that took place during the summer of 2024.
The 2024 renovation resulted in a nearly nine-week closure of LIV.
This extensive upgrade was overseen by the acclaimed experiential design firm ICRAVE.
Steve Lieberman of SJ Lighting played a key role in the 2024 renovation.
The primary objective of the renovation was to reaffirm LIV's position as a global leader in nightlife by introducing groundbreaking technology and enhancing the overall guest experience.
The centerpiece of the renovation was the installation of a custom-built, kinetic LED ceiling affectionately nicknamed "The Spider."
The Spider is a seven-legged, steel truss structure, which alone cost an estimated $3 million.
The Spider contains 410 individual moving LED panels, each capable of rotating at one foot per second in sync with the music.
The Spider is equipped with integrated fans that blow air onto the audience below, adding a tactile dimension to the auditory and visual spectacle.
The renovation also included the addition of over 400 digitally controlled LED panels throughout the venue.
The renovation included new marble floors, granite countertops, and revamped banquettes.
The renovation included rotating art installations by local Miami street artists.
This transformative project underscored LIV's commitment to constant reinvention, aiming to create a truly immersive and unforgettable party experience that sets a new standard for the industry.
The reopening following the 2024 renovation marked a significant milestone.
The reopening was celebrated with a "Sneak Peek Weekend" that featured headlining performances by Travis Scott and Skrillex, signaling a new era for the club.
The official grand opening of LIV was scheduled for early October 2024, confirming that the venue was fully operational and ready to welcome back its elite clientele.
This reopening coincided with the start of LIV's tenth season, celebrating a decade of continuous operation since its 2008 debut.
The timing of the reopening was strategically chosen to capitalize on the peak Miami tourism season.
New programming was introduced, including open-format Fridays, dedicated dance music Saturdays, and "LIV On Sunday" positioned as "the biggest hip-hop party in the world."
The LIV venue continues to host major events throughout the year, including Miami Music Week and Art Basel.
LIV features a roster of the world's top DJs and performers such as DJ Khaled, John Summit, Tiësto, and Lil Wayne, ensuring its relevance and prominence in the global entertainment calendar.
Building on the proven success and strong brand recognition of the Miami flagship, David Grutman embarked on a significant expansion by launching a second LIV nightclub in Las Vegas.

This venture, situated inside the newly constructed Fontainebleau Las Vegas resort, marked a strategic move to replicate the LIV formula in one of the most competitive and saturated nightlife markets in the world.
The Fontainebleau Las Vegas itself is a monumental $3.7 billion development.
The grand opening of Fontainebleau Las Vegas on December 13, 2023, provided the perfect platform for the arrival of its crown jewel nightclub.
The launch of LIV Las Vegas was a carefully orchestrated expansion that aimed to blend the core elements of the Miami concept with the unique energy of the Las Vegas Strip.
Grutman emphasized that artists like resident DJs John Summit and Metro Boomin were involved in the construction phase of LIV Las Vegas.
The involvement of resident DJs John Summit and Metro Boomin made them personally invested in the club's success and ensured a product that reflected their artistic vision.
The LIV Las Vegas venue opened its doors in 2024, quickly establishing itself as a key player in the city's entertainment circuit.
The LIV Las Vegas club operates on a schedule tailored to the Las Vegas market, typically open from Friday to Sunday, from 10:30 p.m. to 4:00 a.m.
From its inception, LIV Las Vegas has focused on delivering an elevated hospitality experience, integrating state-of-the-art lighting and sound systems to compete with the Strip's other mega-clubs.

The LIV Las Vegas venue has attracted a steady stream of high-profile talent, with resident DJs such as John Summit, Metro Boomin, Cloonee, and Dom Dolla performing regularly, alongside special appearances by major artists.
This programming strategy mirrors the successful model employed in Miami, creating a consistent draw for music lovers and club-goers.

The LIV Las Vegas venue has become a magnet for celebrities, welcoming visitors like Bad Bunny during Super Bowl weekend and *Vanderpump Rules* star James Kennedy, who performed as LIV's internationally recognized resident DJ.
This association with celebrity culture helps to generate buzz and reinforces the club's image as a must-visit destination for anyone on the Strip.
The expansion into Las Vegas was about extending Grutman's integrated business ecosystem to a new market.
Similar to the synergy between LIV and the Fontainebleau Miami Beach hotel, the Las Vegas LIV is part of a larger integrated ecosystem.
The Las Vegas LIV ecosystem includes other Groot Hospitality properties co-located within the resort, such as the restaurants Papi Steak and Komodo.

This model allows for cross-promotion and creates a cohesive lifestyle brand where guests can dine and then transition to the nightclub, maximizing revenue opportunities and enhancing the overall guest experience.
Michael Waltman, Executive Vice President of Fontainebleau Development, highlighted this integrated approach.
Michael Waltman explained how the resort aims to capture guests at every stage of their lifecycle, from college attendees entering via guest lists to becoming high-spending VIP clients.
This strategic alignment with the parent company's broader goals demonstrates a well-thought-out plan for sustainable growth and profitability in a hyper-competitive environment.
The launch of LIV Las Vegas represented a significant validation of the LIV brand model.

Successfully adapting the Miami concept to the unique demands of the Las Vegas market proved that the core elements of the brand—luxury, cutting-edge technology, and a focus on top-tier musical talent—were transferable and highly appealing to a new audience.
The timing of the opening of LIV Las Vegas, coinciding with the grand opening of the entire Fontainebleau Las Vegas resort, ensured maximum visibility and media attention.
The initial event for LIV Las Vegas featured A-list celebrities such as Kim Kardashian, Cher, Sylvester Stallone, Lenny Kravitz, Bryan Cranston, Aaron Paul, and Tom Brady.
This star-studded debut sent a clear message to the industry that LIV was not just another club but a major new player poised to make a significant impact.
As of early 2025, LIV Las Vegas remains a prominent fixture on the Strip, continuing to host resident DJs and headline acts.
LIV Las Vegas solidifies its status as a key component of the LIV global brand and a testament to David Grutman's vision for scalable, high-end nightlife experiences.
The LIV Las Vegas venue underwent a months-long renovation, closing November 2024 and reopening March 2025.
The renovation of LIV Las Vegas indicates a continued commitment to maintaining its competitive edge.
LIV nightclub has carved out a distinct and influential niche in the global cultural landscape.
LIV functions as a nexus for celebrity culture, high-energy entertainment, and, at times, high-profile controversy.
LIV's reputation as a magnet for international clientele and global celebrities is well-documented.
Names like Drake, Rihanna, Paris Hilton, and Bad Bunny are frequently cited as regular patrons of LIV.
The concentration of fame at LIV creates a self-perpetuating cycle of allure.
The presence of celebrities attracts more celebrities and media attention, which in turn drives demand from the general public seeking to witness or participate in the spectacle.

LIV has served as a backdrop for countless events, from corporate-sponsored fashion shows for brands like Adidas to elaborate multi-day celebrations for major cultural festivals like Miami Art Week and Miami Music Week.
LIV's role as a backdrop for events further cements its status as a central hub of Miami's social and entertainment scene.

The club's ability to consistently attract and host the world's top DJs and performers, such as Calvin Harris, Diddy, and Machine Gun Kelly, underscores its role as a premier venue for live music and dance culture.
LIV's glamorous facade has been punctuated by a series of notable incidents that have contributed to its controversial reputation.
The club has been the site of several high-profile public feuds and altercations.
One of the earliest documented incidents at LIV involved rapper Dan Blizerian allegedly kicking a woman in the face in December 2014.
Another incident involved a public escalation of tensions between rappers Birdman and Lil Wayne, which culminated in water bottles being thrown at Jim Jones’ birthday party at LIV.
The most widely reported incident occurred outside LIV in December 2014, when Sean "Diddy" Combs allegedly punched Drake over a dispute concerning the beat for Drake's hit song '0 to 100'.
Combs vehemently denied the allegation, calling Drake his friend.
The incident became a major tabloid story and was widely attributed to the LIV venue, further linking the club to celebrity drama.

These events, along with others like Joaquin Phoenix's rap performance tied to his *I'm Still Here* performance art project, paint a picture of LIV as a place where the line between entertainment and reality can blur, leading to unpredictable and sometimes volatile situations.
The most serious documented controversy associated with LIV involves allegations of violent assault.
On November 9, 2024, Miami-based artist and club promoter Prince alleged that rapper Tory Lanez assaulted him inside the LIV nightclub.

According to Prince, the altercation, which originated from a misinterpreted Instagram post, escalated into a brutal attack captured on cellphone video, showing Lanez punching, stomping, and jumping on Prince.
The assault resulted in a dislodged tooth requiring multiple medical procedures and ongoing anxiety for the victim.
Prince's attorney characterized Lanez's conduct as a "chronic problem."
The case proceeded to litigation after failed settlement attempts.
This incident places LIV at the center of a significant legal matter and highlights the club's association with artists facing serious criminal charges.
The controversy was amplified by Megan Thee Stallion's separate accusation against Lanez in July 2024, where she alleged he shot her after a party in Los Angeles.
Megan Thee Stallion's accusation suggests a troubling pattern of alleged behavior that has drawn scrutiny to the environments where these artists perform.
More recently, LIV has continued to be a stage for spontaneous and unexpected events.
In December 2025, pop superstar Shakira performed an impromptu set at the LIV club.
Shakira abruptly ended her performance after reportedly discovering that fans were filming up her dress.
An official statement from the club attributed the interruption to Shakira's own photo/video team filming without consent during an informal crowd interaction, rather than fan behavior.
The incident nonetheless showcased the unpredictable nature of events at the LIV venue.
This mix of world-class entertainment, intense celebrity culture, and recurring controversies makes LIV a compelling and complex subject of cultural analysis.

LIV serves not only as a destination for leisure and celebration but also as a microcosm of the pressures, rivalries, and potential dangers inherent in the high-stakes world of modern celebrity and nightlife.
The "LIV" brand is a potent and valuable asset, built over more than a decade of association with luxury, celebrity, and high-energy entertainment.
LIV's identity is so strong that it has transcended its function as a nightclub name to become a recognizable symbol within the hospitality and entertainment industries.
This strength was formally acknowledged in 2023 when the owners of LIV took legal action to protect their intellectual property from a potentially confusing competitor.
On March 15, 2023, LIV Miami filed a Notice of Opposition with the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) to block the trademark registration of "LIV Golf."
This legal maneuver revealed the commercial significance attached to the four-letter moniker and demonstrated the proactive stance taken by the LIV brand's management to defend its market identity.
In its official filing, LIV argued that the marks "LIV" and "LIV Golf" are confusingly similar not only visually and phonetically but also aurally, creating a high risk of consumer confusion.

The opposition specifically cited the shared use of the term "LIV" and pointed to a common perception among consumers that both brands are connected to the same entity, given the overlapping nature of their target audiences.
LIV's services, centered on nightlife and entertainment, and LIV Golf's services, related to professional golf, were deemed to share an overlapping consumer base.
The overlapping consumer base could lead to the erroneous belief that one brand endorsed or was otherwise associated with the other.
This argument is a standard tactic in trademark law used to prevent dilution of a famous mark and to stop competitors from capitalizing on an existing brand's goodwill.
The case was pending at the time of the article's publication, highlighting the ongoing legal efforts to safeguard the LIV brand's integrity and commercial value.
The origins of the LIV brand name are themselves a key component of its identity, rooted in the history of the Fontainebleau Miami Beach hotel.
The name "LIV" is the Roman numeral for fifty-four (L=50, I=1, V=5).
The name "LIV" is a direct reference to the year 1954, when the original Fontainebleau hotel opened.
This clever wordplay connects the modern nightclub to the property's foundational history, giving the brand a sense of longevity and heritage that distinguishes it from newer establishments.
This historical link is a cornerstone of LIV's marketing and storytelling, reinforcing its position as a timeless yet modern institution in Miami's entertainment scene.

The LIV brand is officially registered with the trademark symbol (®), as seen in its partnership descriptions with institutions like Florida International University, which refers to it as "LIV® nightclub."
This formal registration underscores the LIV brand's legal standing and the seriousness with which its owners treat its protection.

Beyond its legal protections and historical roots, the LIV brand is synonymous with a specific type of experience—a world-class nightlife destination that combines state-of-the-art technology with an exclusive, glamorous atmosphere.
Rankings from publications such as Rolling Stone Magazine, which named it one of the best dance clubs in America, provide third-party validation of LIV's quality and appeal.
Nightclub & Bar Magazine ranked LIV #5 in its 2014 list of the Top 100 Best Clubs in the Country.
Askmen.com ranked LIV as the #2 best club in the world at one point.

These accolades, combined with its consistent billing as "Miami's ultimate nightlife destination" and a venue that "consistently hosts top artists and global celebrities," build a powerful brand identity that is instantly recognizable to those within the industry and aspirational to a global audience.

The LIV brand's identity is thus a composite of its tangible assets—its prime location, its innovative technology, and its successful business model—as well as its intangible qualities: its historical narrative, its exclusive clientele, and its powerful association with the pinnacle of popular culture.
The decision to litigate against LIV Golf is a clear indication that the owners understand the immense value of this carefully constructed identity and are prepared to defend it vigorously.

Miami Beach’s hottest nightclub is finally reopening. Here’s what we know so far
================================================================================

By [Madeleine Marr](https://www.miamiherald.com/profile/218644725/)

Updated April 18, 2021 9:25 PM ![Image 11: Gift Icon](https://www.miamiherald.com/-ilszyoonb/data/giftArticle/giftIcon.png)Gift Article

      ![Image 12: LIV](https://www.miamiherald.com/miami-com/nightlife/article250629644.html)

LIV THE MIAMI HERALD

It’s go time.

In another sign things are returning back to “normal,” Miami Beach’s hottest club, [LIV](https://www.livnightclub.com/), is reopening Friday.

Owner David Grutman announced the big news Monday on social media.

The grand opening weekend at the Fontainebleau Hotel hot spot includes big time performers hitting the DJ booth at LIV, which [closed back in March 2020](https://www.miamiherald.com/miami-com/miami-com-news/article241130766.html) after the pandemic hit.

At the time, Grutman released a statement saying he was pausing operations out of an abundance of caution” and “following the guidelines of local and national and international authorities.”

November 3, 2020 2:43 PM

Story, Grutman’s other nightclub in Miami Beach, remains closed due to the ongoing coronavirus pandemic. But his festive foodie magnet restaurants which include [Komodo](https://www.miamiherald.com/miami-com/restaurants/article225803575.html), [Swan Miami](https://www.miamiherald.com/miami-com/things-to-do/article225810755.html) and [Papi Steak](https://www.miamiherald.com/miami-com/miami-com-news/article234189562.html) have been up and running for months.

##### Read Next

###### [Where To Stay](https://www.miamiherald.com/miami-com/hotels-motels "Where To Stay")

### [Can these celebs make this South Beach street cool again? Their new hotel is a start](https://www.miamiherald.com/miami-com/hotels-motels/article246804897.html#storylink=readmore_inline "Can these celebs make this South Beach street cool again? Their new hotel is a start ")

October 29, 2020 3:38 PM

On LIV’s website is a picture of Alesso, with the headline, “Together Again.” General admission tickets for females start at $250 (male tickets are sold out). A dance floor table at the 18,000 square foot club runs you $15,000; festivities begin at 11 p.m.

On Saturday, house producer duo the Martinez Brothers will make an appearance and Sunday it’s “Love & Hip Hop” star DJ Stevie J and rapper Don P.

There are no other events for the month on LIV’s calendar.

How late can you stay out? After weeks of wild spring break partying, Miami-Dade County’s [nightly curfew](https://www.miamiherald.com/news/local/community/miami-dade/miami-beach/article250507634.html) ended Monday.

Florida is currently in Phase 3 of its COVID reopening plans, Gov. Ron DeSantis said back in September.

The Miami Herald reached out to get more details of the reopening and how the venue will be adhering to [CDC guidelines](https://www.cdc.gov/coronavirus/2019-ncov/index.html), but did not immediately hear back.

This story was originally published April 13, 2021 at 10:38 AM.

Nightlife

 

Overview Meetings 

* * *

#### A Night at LIV at the Fontainebleau

There are few things that compare to a night out at LIV. Grab your friends, dress to impress, and dance and drink the night away with some of Miami's most beautiful people. When you do, you might even run into a celebrity. Rumor has it LIV is popular amongst famous faces when they're in town like Jonathan Cheban, Drake, Rihanna and Paris Hilton.

#### About LIV

At LIV, you'll get the real Miami nightlife experience. Located on the bottom level of the Fontainebleau Miami Beach Hotel, and occupying more than 18,000 square feet of space, LIV combines an ultra exclusive lounge with a high-energy nightclub.

LIV offers three full-service bars helmed by some of the best mixologists in the business. For the ultimate VIP treatment, guests can reserve up to fifty banquette areas or six private skyboxes, each featuring table service.

#### Hot Parties and DJs

Five nights a week, LIV has some of the hottest DJs and performers on the music scene, from David Guetta and Calvin Harris, to MAKJ, Mr. Mauricio, Luciano, Audien, D-Nice, Burns and more.

#### General Information

LIV is open Wednesdays through Sundays, from 11 p.m. to 5 a.m. It offers VIP tables, private skyboxes, three full-service bars and a lavish main dance floor. Guests must be 21+ with a valid I.D.

 Accountability and transparency are core values at the Wikimedia Foundation. We manage funds and resources to ensure that every contribution supports our mission. We have earned the Platinum Seal of Transparency from Candid (formerly GuideStar), and Charity Navigator awarded us its highest rating. You can [read our most recent annual report](https://annual.wikimedia.org/) for more information about our financial health. 

45% Investment in Technology 
Nearly half of our budget goes toward supporting the technology that powers Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects. We are constantly working to enhance the user experience for both contributors and readers, improve site security, and ensure reliable access to our websites globally. This infrastructure and product support sustain one of the top ten most visited websites in the world, all at a fraction of the cost of popular for-profit websites.

34% Support for Volunteers 
The global reach of Wikimedia projects is made possible by the hard work of volunteers from across the globe. We provide grants, legal support, and other resources to help build vibrant volunteer communities. Additionally, we promote community engagement through outreach initiatives and advocate for the growth and protection of free knowledge.

12% General and Administrative Expenses 
Operational costs are essential for the smooth management and governance of the Wikimedia Foundation. These expenses help us recruit top talent and support staff around the world, empowering them to carry out the mission of the Wikimedia Foundation.

11% Allocation to Fundraising Efforts 
Donor support is crucial to sustaining Wikipedia and our other free knowledge endeavors. Our team is committed to efficient and effective fundraising throughout the year, ensuring that every contribution helps advance our mission.

LIV ON SUNDAY **Event Details:**  
– **Date:** Sunday, August 31, 2025  
– **Time:** Doors open at 11:30 PM  
– **Location:** [LIV Nightclub Miami](https://www.livnightclub.com/miami), 4441 Collins Ave, Miami Beach, FL  
– **Age Requirement:** 21 & over

Wrap up your weekend in true Miami style as **Boston Richey** takes over **LIV Nightclub Miami** on Sunday, August 31, 2025. Known for his melodic rap flows, street-driven lyrics, and rapidly rising profile in hip-hop, Boston Richey is set to deliver a high-energy night inside one of the world's most iconic nightlife venues. Fans can expect an unforgettable experience filled with his breakout anthems, collaborations, and undeniable stage presence that has earned him recognition as one of rap's fastest-growing stars.

**About Boston Richey**

Hailing from Tallahassee, Florida, Boston Richey has built a reputation as one of hip-hop's most promising new voices. His unique style blends melodic hooks with raw storytelling, creating tracks that resonate with audiences across the country. Songs like "Keep Dissing," "Bullseye 2," and "Public Housing" have earned him millions of streams while collaborations with heavyweights like Future and Lil Durk have solidified his position in today's rap landscape. His music continues to rise on major streaming platforms, making him a must-see artist for hip-hop fans. Listen to Boston Richey on [Spotify](https://open.spotify.com/artist/3x8mY8XKaUxuwHXH4TTiBb) and [Apple Music](https://music.apple.com/us/artist/real-boston-richey/1593037249).

Located inside the legendary [Fontainebleau Miami Beach](https://www.fontainebleau.com/nightlife/liv), LIV is internationally recognized for its unmatched nightlife experience. Featuring state-of-the-art production, luxury VIP seating, and a vibrant party atmosphere, LIV consistently hosts top artists and global celebrities, cementing its reputation as Miami's ultimate nightlife destination.

Make the night unforgettable with a [VIP table](https://www.livnightclub.com/miami/table-reservations), which includes premium bottle service, luxury seating, and prime views of the stage. This event is 21+ only. A valid government-issued ID is required for entry. Fashionable nightlife attire is strongly encouraged.

[Book online](https://www.livnightclub.com/miami/events/)

Written by Kat Bein

Advertising

### Time Out says

LIV has been leading the pack in Miami’s club scene since it debuted in 2008 as the crown jewel of the Fontainebleau Hotel’s unprecedented billion-dollar renovation. With top-tier talent (Skrillex and Bieber once performed in the same weekend) and insane six-figure bottle service (Mark Cuban allegedly dropped more than 100 grand on a single bottle of champagne in 2013), LIV quickly showed the nightlife world that Miami’s best days are not in the past. “Our grand opening was for the Victoria’s Secret fashion show and, each night since, we’ve continued to change production and create a new party on a nightly basis,” says owner David Grutman.

But even the giants must learn to adapt. And one of LIV’s biggest challenges came last summer as the club closed for months to undergo a $10 million renovation. “We’ll never stay complacent,” says Grutman, referring to the overhaul that added more than 400 digitally controlled LED panels to create choreographed light shows that take up the club’s entire domed ceiling. On its sneak-peek weekend—in typical star-studded fashion—Travis Scott, Skrillex and Lil Wayne performed on the brand-new stage. “The new look gives fans more of a 360-degree experience, and you’ll know what I mean once you’ve experienced it,” says Grutman, hinting at a shift in programming. “The world changes on a constant basis, and so does music. Fridays will remain open format, Saturday we’ll have dance music and LIV On Sunday remains the biggest hip-hop party in the world, but we have new surprises on Wednesday and Thursday that will launch in the next couple months.”

[Amber Sampson](https://lasvegasweekly.com/staff/amber-sampson/ "Amber Sampson staff page")

Thu, Nov 21, 2024 (2 a.m.)

It’s just after midnight at LIV Nightclub. Throngs of bodies pack the dancefloor, bottle girls shoulder bright neon signs emblazoned with “Scorpio SZN” and I’m sharing a section with _Vanderpump Rules_ reality TV star James Kennedy. My head’s on a swivel searching for cameras—_Could this be season 12? Is this the show’s next ceremonious Vegas episode playing out?_ But unlike what I’m used to seeing Kennedy stir up on screen, there’s very little drama. Instead, the internationally recognized resident DJ of LIV has hopped behind the decks to deliver, in true _Vanderpump_ fashion, one of the best days of our lives.

Newly acquainted strangers smush and grind together to his mashup of Icona Pop’s “I Love It” and Rihanna’s “Bitch Better Have My Money.” And it’s almost instinctual how the hands go up for Kendrick Lamar’s “Not Like Us,” which Kennedy seamlessly transitions into a remix of M83’s “Midnight City.” Pretty soon, he’s ditching his t-shirt and scaling the DJ booth to sing along with his fans.

Within its first year on the Strip, LIV Nightclub and LIV Beach have orchestrated countless moments like this, drawing the likes of Kehlani, Tiësto, Calvin Harris, John Summit, Dom Dolla, Busta Rhymes and plenty more through its doors. And nightlife impresario David Grutman of Groot Hospitality isn’t finished making his mark on Las Vegas.

“Coming into a market where you have the best operators in the world all condensed into one area, and just to be able to open in that kind of marketplace, for me, was a very humbling experience,” says Grutman, who opened the original LIV Nightclub at Fontainebleau in Miami 16 years ago.

“We went a little bit of a different route with some of our DJs, and it was so great to see John Summit, Metro Boomin, Cloonee and Dom Dolla all have record years,” he continues. “We’re pretty good at projecting people’s trajectory and to see how those guys just took off is incredible.”

Grutman says stakes were incredibly high in the first year, launching LIV in a hyper competitive nightlife town. He leaned heavily on his Las Vegas team to help navigate the scene, knowing that what worked well on the East Coast didn’t always translate well to the West.

“The hospitality, a lot of the lighting and sound and stuff like that, we elevated it for the Vegas market,” he says. “But one thing that we were able to work even better in Vegas is the ecosystem, because we have \[restaurants\] Papi Steak and Komodo. …We really wanted to be that full ecosystem where you come and have dinner and then you could take that and go to the nightclub afterwards.”

That strategy has helped bolster business all around at Fontainebleau, and quickly established LIV as the place to be. During Super Bowl weekend, Bad Bunny popped in. And where else could you catch a club residency by Metro Boomin this year?

“Also seeing those days of John Summit, and it’s like 90% female, is crazy to me,” Grutman says. “I’ve never seen a nightclub that’s 90% female before in my life. John Summit is definitely America’s sweetheart, that’s for sure.”

Grutman says it’s even more impactful to see these artists flourish at LIV because they were there from the beginning.

“They were walking the property with me when it was under construction,” Grutman says, “and I was like, ‘I swear to you, this ceiling is going to move around, this and that.’ And they’d see workers and builders and duct tape. So to see it come alive, I feel like they take it so personal. They feel like they were a part of the success of LIV, especially in the first year.”

During Formula 1 race week, LIV will host a wealth of nightlife programming, including performances by Dom Dolla and Cloonee at LIV on the Grid and a trackside hospitality experience called Papi Steak Garage. Grutman says more resident artists will also be announced for the clubs soon to ensure the momentum keeps building.

“The level of hospitality here ... It’s like nothing else I’ve ever seen,” he says. “Vegas has the best of the best. I’m just so happy to even be there with these guys and to be able to play on the same field.”

**LIV Nightclub** _Fontainebleau Las Vegas, 702-678-9700, [livnightclub.com](https://livnightclub.com/). Friday-Sunday, 10:30p.m.-4 a.m._

June 21, 2024

Tips To Stay Ahead in the Nightlife Industry
--------------------------------------------

What’s next in nightlife? A session at HD Expo + Conference 2024 covers what we need to know

Words by: Stephanie Chen • Photos courtesy of Fontainebleau Development + PWP Studio

Today’s nightlife scene combines food, beverage, and talent. Are you keeping up with the changing, social media-fueled environment?

Five industry authorities (**Philip Loomis** of Drai’s Beachclub, **Mike Snedegar** of Mike Snedegar Consulting, **Christopher LaPorte** of RESET, **Michael Waltman** of Fontainebleau Development, and **Jennie Yip** of Jenjuice Hospitality and COHJO) weighed in on exactly where the industry is headed at [HD Expo + Conference 2024](https://hdexpo.hospitalitydesign.com/press-release/celebrating-the-success-of-hd-expo-conference-2024-more-than-11000-total-attendees-and-600-exhibitors-came-together-for-three-days-of-discovery-learning-and-networking/) during the _I Love the Nightlife: Shifts in Cocktailing and Afterhours_ session.

Here are six takeaways from the conversation:

### 1\. Guests are looking for an all-in-one experience

More people are being drawn to venues where they can have multiple experiences under one roof. “What you’re starting to see now is ‘How can I do everything in one night?’” says Waltman. “How can I get a great meal, dance, and have great cocktails? How can I get that bottle experience all while at one table? At Papi Steak, for instance, we’ve taken components from nightlife and trickled them down into the restaurant. People are gravitating towards that—they appreciate having their space at the table, and even if the music is loud, they can still have a conversation.”

### 2\. Maintain a long-term ecosystem with clients

“When college kids come into town, they might be coming through a guest list or buying a GA ticket, but we wrap our arms around them because staying at Fontainebleau or Wynn is aspirational,” Waltman says. “At that point, in college, they might be four to a room at a motel, but we keep them in our ecosystem with a promoter. They graduate college, they get a job. Next thing you know, they might be a fourth tier table. We’ve seen it happen over the years. Then that person ends up working on Wall Street and becomes a $20,000 a night customer. Having appreciation for everybody that comes in here, and knowing that it’s a long-term play, is something that we’ve learned over the course of time to be successful.”

### 3\. Design capturable moments

Whether it’s younger partygoers or older guests, everyone is looking for a memorable experience. Younger clientele tend to look for “that camera phone type moment,” says Snedegar. “Many are less interested in bottle service and more about the experience.”

Meanwhile, “the nightlife-educated customer is maturing into a higher net worth, so they’re going to go after a more luxe experience,” says Loomis. “But people still want to be in a place where they can be seen and post on social media because social media is working its way up into the older generations as well. So it is about a moment.”

### 4\. Find your brand ambassadors

Know your audience and they’ll do the talking for you. “We’re seeing more and more individualized experiences and venues, where you have to be creative in knowing who your customer is and bring something special to that unique segment,” says LaPorte.

Whether it’s guests looking for non-alcoholic options or cannabis lounges, know your niche and cater to them. “It’s just a matter of finding who that consumer is,” LaPorte adds. “Know who you are, know what your product is, find your same people, let those people be your ambassadors.”

Brand ambassadors are not only limited to guests, but also extend to staff. “It’s hiring individuals that understand operations and what we want,” says Yip. “It’s about creating a culture and then within that, create ambassadors—your managers are your ambassadors.”

### 5\. Create touchpoints and personalized experiences

“The entire experience matters,” Yip says. “From the time guests make a reservation to the time they come through the door, who are they going to see? How are they going to remember this space? How does a drink feel and taste?”

These touchpoints will only need to become more personalized in the future. “Today, we have Resy and OpenTable, but the future will be more one-on-one,” Yip adds. “There will be influencer apps. People want to find their own passionate communities, their own people that like a particular martini that can be created within Fontainebleau or Drai’s. And the customization of technology is going to change that.”

### 6\. Embrace exclusivity

“A lot of people want to do things with like-minded people, but they don’t want to go to a huge nightclub—they want something that’s going to be their own,” says LaPorte. “So I’m very confident in the members-only model. We’re seeing one open up in downtown Las Vegas very soon, and I have a lot of confidence in that being successful.”

Waltman expands on this by calling out Fontainebleau’s private club, Poodle Room. “We have a really long list of people trying to get in, but all we’re doing is curating who’s up there,” he says. “People love the fact that it’s not full, and that they can recognize the person across the room. There are no cameras. There’s definitely a niche where people are willing to pay just to be in something that’s exclusive that they can hang their hat on.”

The no-camera policy is gaining popularity. “What’s interesting is that along with the rise of the members club, are also spaces that do not allow photo and video,” adds Snedegar. “Pinky Ring at Bellagio, for instance, has a no phone policy, which adds to the experience because everybody is connected to the energy of the room.”

Legendary LIV Club Isn’t Sure When It Will Reopen
=================================================

![Image 3: Crystal Gross](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/26553e0f19a351d81b811ac5a306c42b162b09c498e8a215609d1566f0443782?s=80&d=mm&r=r) by [Crystal Gross](https://balleralert.com/profiles/blogs/author/crystal-gross/)

[October 19, 2020](https://balleralert.com/profiles/blogs/liv-club-miami-not-sure-reopen/)

in [News](https://balleralert.com/profiles/blogs/category/news/)

Reading Time: 3 mins read

[![Image 4: Legendary LIV Club Isn’t Sure When It Will Reopen](https://balleralert.com/wp-content/themes/jnews/assets/img/jeg-empty.png) (Photo by John Parra/Getty Images for BET)](https://i0.wp.com/balleralert.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/10/GettyImages-1052324378-scaled.jpg?fit=2560%2C1707&ssl=1)

The infamous Miami night club LIV remains shut down due to the coronavirus but also due to the power struggle between state and local government.

According to _Newsbreak_, the surge of the virus is what both would like to control. And although the club can open under the state’s Governor Ron DeSantis’ September 25 Order that allows nightclubs to reopen at 50% capacity, Miami official’s midnight curfew has halted the process.

LIV is known for its glamour and star-studded parties. The list of attendees is endless but includes high rollers like Drake, Kanye West, and Rick Ross who have shouted out the club in their songs. People pay a pretty penny to just get in–one big stepper spent $20,000 just to get a table, while another dished out $120,000 just to sit on the DJ booth while Cardi B performed back in February.

But now, its sleek black floors and snakeskin couches once surrounded by throngs of party-goers has been replaced with an eerie silence. LIV owner David Grutman, 46, says he’s “cried real tears” since his club has been shut down and tried to stay away as much as he can.

“It’s really been my lifeblood,” he added.

City officials are also restricting loud music, which is another reason LIV hasn’t reopened its doors. Officials say they don’t want people shouting which could risk the spread of the virus through their spit. On top of that, they also have required masks to be worn unless people are eating and drinking.

“We take a more cautious approach here in Miami-Dade,” Miami-Dade County Mayor Carlos Gimenez said recently. He warned: “We are still not out of the woods.”

Grutman doesn’t want to risk spreading the virus and also blames the curfew for his reason to not reopen LIV or his other nightclub, Story. “We’re going to open it when we can give the right experience,” he said. “I’m not into giving half-ass experiences.”

Florida’s Republican governor Ron DeSantis seems pretty eager to reopen its economy, despite the states reported 15,000 deaths. But people like Grutman have witnessed the revolving door of openings and closings, and feel it’s not worth it.

Grutman is also the owner of several restaurants and co-owns one with producer Pharrell, including Komodo, a hangout patronized by celebrities. According to the news outlet, all were shut down back in March.

When the governor gave the go-ahead to reopen in June, Grutman decided to do so, but he now regrets that decision. “We thought the world was back,” Grutman said. “I was naive enough to think that we’d turned the corner.” Six weeks later he shut the doors after cases of the virus spiked. South Florida quickly became a coronavirus hotspot as 12,000-15,000 new cases per day were reported.

“We were allowed to reopen and bars were not, yet people were drinking like crazy at our place, so it was one of those mixed-signal things. It built up a lot of animosity,” he said.

It’s safe to say Grutman’s LIV has taken a tremendous hit–on big weekends, the club can make $1 million in one night. It was the place to be after the Kansas City Chiefs won the 2020 Super Bowl. It’s also been the home of Victoria Secret’s 2009 fashion show. And no matter who or how many calls the owner receives, he’s sticking to his guns and not budging to reopen. Instead, he’s spending his time trying to install five-minute rapid testing and adding ultraviolet disinfecting lights to the vents. He still believes, however, that a vaccine is the only safety net in terms of big club events.

“Everybody has their own ideas of what’s going to happen, second wave, no second wave,” he said.

LIV at Fontainebleau, consistently ranked one of the top nightlife venues in the world, reopened after a $10 million renovation to kick off the nightclub’s tenth season. LIV has redefined nightlife on Miami Beach and pioneered the nightlife experience. David Grutman owner of Groot Hospitality, retained acclaimed experiential design firm ICRAVE to oversee the transformation.  With over 18,000 square feet of striking architecture, soaring ceilings, vibrant lighting and its iconic dome. LIV will continue to set the stage for the ultimate nightlife experience.

LIV has been updated to reflect the latest in technology and design in the nightlife industry. The physical and technological upgrades incorporate the latest and greatest available including maximizing the historic ‘bones’ of the space and have transformed the iconic dome and steel truss – affectionately referred to as ‘The Spider’. LIV has become an even more immersive and energetic nightclub environment. This, along with a general refresh of the look and materials, and the introduction of projection mapping in the space, have further cemented LIV as the go-to club in Miami and beyond.

LIV’s footprint stands in the home of the world-renowned Tropigala Lounge, known in the 50’s and 60’s as the La Ronde Room. Frank Sinatra was the first to illuminate the stage, followed by the likes of Sammy Davis Jr., Ann Miller, Elvis Presley and Tony Bennet. LIV has once again made the space an epicenter for style, fame and glamour.

15.title: VGhlIE5pbmUgV2VpcmRlc3QgVGhpbmdzIHRvIEV2ZXIgSGFwcGVuIEluc2lkZSBMSVY=
15.content:
In just a short period of time, LIV has become a near-unparalleled hegemonic force in Miami nightlife and culture. Since the club’s 2008 opening within the foundations of the Fontainebleau Hotel, LIV has grown considerably from operating solely as Miami’s premiere den of upper crust hedonism. As its world-famous clientele can attest to, LIV is an international destination, a safe place where your favorite rapper can wreck the dance floor while your most beloved basketball player indiscriminately burns through several hundred dollars’ worth of champagne.

But as anyone who has ever watched a VH1 _Behind the Music_ documentary knows, it takes more than drug and drink-fueled debauchery to reach the top. Beyond the grit and moxie necessary to make it in the cutthroat Miami club scene, it also takes a fair bit of insanity. You don’t get to be consistently ranked as one of the world’s top clubs without offering something resembling an unforgettable experience.

And when people let loose and champagne flows, strange shit is likely to go down. Below, we have compiled the nine weirdest things to have ever happened at LIV. While some of these incidents have made us laugh and some have made us cringe, each has managed to make _New Times_ drop our collective jaw and run to our keyboards.   
**9. When Eric Butkiewicz gave Miami its most American mug shot ever.**   
Ah, America: a wonderful place where citizens enjoy the privilege of choosing between a malleable corporate shill and a bigoted quasi-fascist to lead the country for the next four years. Isn’t it grand? We Americans have a proud tradition of annually celebrating our freedoms on our national day of independence, July 4. However, on July 4, 2012, one LIV attendee may have embraced America’s free market principles a bit too zealously. Clad in red, white and blue face paint demonstrating his love for the good ol‘ US of A, then-31-year-old [Eric Oram Butkiewicz was arrested by Miami Beach police](https://www.miaminewtimes.com/news/eric-butkiewicz-man-in-american-flag-face-mug-shot-was-arrested-for-selling-xanax-at-club-liv-on-july-4-6523328) for peddling Xanax during LIV’s fourth of July festivities. As detailed in the police report, Butkiewicz told officers the following: “I possibly have three Xanax bars in my possession.” Ever the cunning entrepreneur, Butkiewicz actually had 13 in his possesion. For embodying both the proud patriotic ideals and adventurous spirit that have made our country great, we salute Butkiewicz for being the rebel we need, although perhaps not the one we deserve. (_Miami New Times_ does not endorse the sale or consumption of illegal narcotics.)
